question: What follows if aggregated atoms do not truly mingle their own natures?
premises: Aggregation may imply mingling of natures.
If no such mingling occurs, aggregation is superficial.
Without true mingling, form cannot be established.
inference: If atoms do not mingle in nature, the result would be formlessness.
plain_english: If there is no real mingling of their own natures, then what results would be formlessness.
